title: Critical path to M7: execution plan for launching the design partner's three sites directly on the shared tier
description:
Why: Ryan (2026-11-08): launching a site must be a data change only (no code edit, no deploy). M7 is the first milestone at which that is true on production, so M7 is the gate for every new shared-tier site, including the design partner's three sites (PPY-37f2ec). The partner's three sites launch DIRECTLY on the shared tier at M7 as tenant deployments created by data (Ryan, 2026-11-08, repeated): never dedicated first, no later move. M7 therefore contains everything they need: data-only provisioning from a deployment record, shared sign-in, branding and layout as data (preset, SiteConfig, BrandPack, starter template), lifecycle, export and deletion, cost accounting basics, and the isolation and review gates. Estimates are in agent sessions (one session = one agent, 2 to 4 hours, one reviewed PR).

(a) CRITICAL PATH to M7. Three chains of similar length; all three are managed as critical.
1. Isolation chain, about 15 sessions in sequence: auth spike PPY-9f3de0 (parts PPY-867f76 and PPY-f4d892 in parallel) -> session claims PPY-0bb0fd -> functions take the tenant from the caller PPY-7dc463 (part 1 PPY-cc8a4c, then three parallel parts) -> workers and operators PPY-203ce2 -> group rules removed PPY-bdc4ee (also waits on the data chain: tenantId PPY-94d609 -> key prefixes PPY-ce6207, PPY-752480, PPY-f60a1e, PPY-ef2c57 -> adoption tools PPY-8f9462) -> security gate 1 PPY-3ff465 -> TI rehearsal PPY-e1d26f -> TI cut-over PPY-e51189 -> M7.
2. Layout chain, about 16 sessions: card and brand pack slices PPY-ecb656, PPY-7bc5b7 -> rest of PPY-613a29 and PPY-88a883 -> publication preset PPY-cf7e6e (about 8 sessions, the largest single item) -> TI brand-neutral acceptance PPY-7e396d -> TI cut-over; and preset -> starter template PPY-3aa10f -> provisioning PPY-70a429 -> provisioning security review PPY-1da916 -> M7.
3. Prospectus chain, about 11 Papyrus sessions plus Prospectus work and Ryan's approvals: Prospectus answers (PPY-6d9a6d, answered by epic kanbus-b770c2) -> deployment records and API kanbus-271b4a + shared sign-in bound to a deployment kanbus-3e5e82 (Prospectus session) -> Papyrus consumer PPY-966ef5 -> provisioning PPY-70a429 -> joint security review PPY-1da916 with kanbus-fa72e8 -> M7; and lifecycle events kanbus-6efecd + billing standing kanbus-b19d5a -> PPY-6cb44b -> lifecycle states PPY-d7274f -> deletion PPY-62f10d.
NOT on the path to M7: the tenant listing indexes PPY-1ce06f must merge before the shared stack's first create but are short; native tokens and the scaler PPY-2a44b2 and the ordering rule PPY-c446fe (D4); bring-your-own Google client PPY-496c0b and its spike PPY-8eca5b; overage billing PPY-8a3c6a; TI's 14-day green close PPY-16f13a (D3); dedicated-site adoption PPY-13fbea; managed upgrades PPY-297ebe; the cost model PPY-04ce84; preview PPY-91fb68, home templates PPY-b21340, onboarding PPY-810f42; reader features PPY-6b084f, PPY-5219fc, PPY-d0a3d5, PPY-1f83a6 (D6).

(b) PARALLEL TRACKS and what can start today (no blockers, one session each; dispatch list in the first comment):
- Isolation and auth: PPY-867f76, PPY-f4d892 (auth spike parts), PPY-65e5a9 (suite generator), PPY-46635e (tenancy mode switch). Next: PPY-cc8a4c, PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-06ae68.
- Data model: PPY-cd5926 (inventory), PPY-94d609 (tenantId fields), PPY-31c45c (Tenant, membership, domain), PPY-8f2c4f (GSI ledger). Next: PPY-c020ce, PPY-9f929e, then the key tasks (split by model group when dispatched).
- Serving and edge: PPY-7cd7a2 (CDN spike part 1), PPY-16d75b (output prefix). Next: PPY-8891e2, PPY-1d5b1a, then PPY-3bbbf9 after the spike.
- Site as data and brand: PPY-ee1e02 (SiteConfig schema), PPY-ecb656 (cards), PPY-7bc5b7 (brand pack validator).
- Metering and cost: PPY-f98e05 (cost tags with the Prospectus package's applyCostTags/assertCostTags). Token reports need a Python twin of the UsageSender (Prospectus kanbus-40dc2a) and the papyrus queue switched on (kanbus-71ff98, Ryan's approval).
- Prospectus (Prospectus session, never edited from here): kanbus-271b4a, kanbus-3e5e82, kanbus-6efecd, kanbus-b19d5a, kanbus-f45f7f, kanbus-fa72e8, kanbus-6daa8f; Papyrus asks recorded on PPY-966ef5.
- Sign-in: PPY-fdbbd7 after claims and the newsroom host PPY-130eb2.
- TI dogfood: on the path (cut-over before M7); rehearsal after PPY-bdc4ee.

(c) SPIKES FIRST (all start today):
- Access-rule claims PPY-9f3de0 (two sessions in parallel, time box 3 days). Fallback if it fails: tenant models reached only through custom queries and mutations whose resolvers read the claims (adds about 6 to 8 sessions to the isolation chain; decide the same day).
- CloudFront PPY-3b3cc3 (PPY-7cd7a2 today, PPY-8891e2; time box 3 days). Fallbacks: if a purge cannot be limited to one tenant, freshness is TTL-only with versioned object keys; if multi-tenant distributions do not fit, one distribution with one certificate per custom domain, sharded when the alternate-name quota binds.
- Prospectus PPY-6d9a6d: closed 2026-11-08; answers mapped on the issue. Fallback if API-created deployments slip: an operator route in Prospectus that creates the deployment record as data (still no file edit, no deploy).
- Cognito Google clients PPY-8eca5b (2 days): off the path; only bring-your-own clients depend on it.

(d) DATA-ONLY PROVISIONING FLOW (target at M7; details in the design note):
1. An operator (for the partner) or, from M8, self-serve checkout creates deployment <site> of product papyrus for an Account through the Prospectus API (kanbus-271b4a), idempotent by operation id. Prospectus is the only writer of deployment records.
2. Prospectus publishes deployment.changed (ask on PPY-966ef5, via kanbus-6efecd); Papyrus also runs a reconcile sweep over deployments changed since its cursor, so a lost event only delays.
3. Papyrus's provisioning workflow (PPY-70a429) re-reads the deployment and the Account's entitlement from Prospectus (never trusts the event body), checks rate limits and the reserved-name list (PPY-1da916), then creates the Tenant, the owner's TenantMembership, TenantDomain <site>.p.apyr.us and its edge host entry, SiteDocuments from the starter template, sections, corpus, Cyclotron id and usage counters, and queues the first projection. Every step idempotent and audited outside tenant data.
4. The owner opens <site>.p.apyr.us/newsroom, is sent to newsroom.p.apyr.us, signs in with the shared Google client; Prospectus authorize checks the token is bound to that deployment and the person is a member (kanbus-3e5e82); the pre-token Lambda issues role claims.
Nothing in this flow edits a file, deploys, changes the Cognito callback list or issues a certificate (the wildcard covers <site>.p.apyr.us).

(e) INTEGRATION AND RELEASE ORDER (one new index per existing table per deploy; releases by the newsroom automation session; dedicated sites take releases only when bumped):
- R1: PPY-46635e, PPY-94d609, new tables PPY-31c45c, PPY-c020ce, PPY-9f929e, PPY-8f2c4f, PPY-16d75b, PPY-1d5b1a, PPY-f98e05, PPY-ee1e02, PPY-7bc5b7, PPY-ecb656. All additive.
- R2: PPY-0bb0fd, PPY-06ae68, PPY-7dc463, and PPY-1ce06f (one index on each of about nine tables; never with another index change on those tables; Reference's publicFeedKey ships in a different release).
- R3: key-prefix writers with dual read PPY-ce6207, PPY-752480, PPY-f60a1e, PPY-ef2c57; adoption PPY-8f9462.
- Shared stack first create (staging, then production) PPY-daf673 after R3.
- R4: PPY-98eaee, PPY-203ce2, PPY-baa75d, PPY-e01d82, PPY-3bbbf9, PPY-82de58, PPY-ca247b, PPY-130eb2, PPY-fdbbd7, PPY-413576, PPY-e572de.
- R5: PPY-bdc4ee and PPY-b99fc0, shared stack only, after the suite is green twice and gate 1.
- Then provisioning, lifecycle, export, deletion, metering, each additive; then the partner's three deployments (PPY-37f2ec).

(f) SCHEDULE (assumptions: six Papyrus agents plus one Prospectus agent; about two sessions per agent per working day; same-day merges to develop; a release every one to two days; Ryan answers approvals within a day; spikes succeed; about 135 sessions in the M7 scope):
- M0 2 to 3 days; M1 1 to 2 weeks alongside; M2 about 1.5 weeks; M3 about 1 week after M2; M4 about 1 week overlapping M3; TI cut-over 2 to 3 days after M3 and M4; M6 overlaps M4 and M5; M7 about 1 week after the cut-over if Prospectus's deployment API, shared sign-in and lifecycle events have landed.
- Earliest realistic M7 about 5 weeks out (around 2026-12-11); optimistic 2026-12-02; pessimistic late January 2027.
- Pull in: keep D4 and D6 off the path; operator-triggered partner deployments so Stripe checkout is not a gate; split the key tasks across more agents; book the external review now (it is a gate for the partner's sites at M7 by default, D22).
- Push out: auth spike failure (1 to 2 weeks); Prospectus capacity or approval delays (three Prospectus changes are on the path); preset scope creep; new-account setup (Google OAuth, SES, quotas); Amplify deploy failures; review findings.

(g) RYAN'S APPROVALS, in order: answer the open decisions (design note); create the shared stack's AWS account (recommended papyrus-shared) with SSO for agents; create the shared Google OAuth client and enter its id and secret yourself; approve wildcard certificates *.p.apyr.us and *.staging.p.apyr.us; approve the Prospectus usage queue and Papyrus's send permission (kanbus-71ff98); approve the Prospectus deployment API's new permissions (kanbus-fa72e8 item 9); sign off gate 1 (PPY-3ff465); approve TI's cut-over day; approve creating the partner's three shared-tier deployments. Early and off the path: submit p.apyr.us to the Public Suffix List.

Milestones and their Gherkin acceptance: epic PPY-6a6357 (M0 to M8).
